seo.title: Homeless help in Phoenix - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Phoenix: shelter, heat safety, meals, health care, benefits, work, identification, and legal support.

page.heading: Phoenix homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, fire, overdose, or medical emergency: 911 Shelter and local services: 211 or 877-211-8661 Single-adult shelter access: 602-883-4509 or 602-229-5155 Mental-health or substance-use crisis: call or text 988, or call 844-534-4673 Domestic-violence shelter screening: 480-890-3039 or 844-723-3387
page.notice: Beds, meals, funding, transport, hours, and eligibility can change. Call or check the linked provider page before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, payment, document, benefit, ride, or job. Call 911 for immediate danger or a life-threatening medical emergency.
page.intro:
Phoenix uses separate access routes for single adults, families, young people, veterans, and survivors of domestic violence. Tell staff your age, household members, exact location, health or mobility needs, pregnancy, veteran status, service animal or pet, and whether you are safe tonight.
Best first step for a single adult: go to the Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S. 12th Avenue, or call first. The facility is open 24 hours; Keys to Change publishes assessment and service-plan hours of 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. CASS beds are assigned in person, first come and first served; they cannot be reserved by phone or email.
page.footer: No Home Help provides practical signposting, not emergency response, legal advice, medical advice, or a guarantee of service.

categories.title: Urgent help, outreach, and extreme heat

entries.title: Emergency services — 911
entries.description:
Phone: 911.
Call for immediate violence, fire, heat stroke, overdose, unconsciousness, severe breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, serious injury, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark and describe the danger first.
City of Phoenix — Office of Homeless Solutions

entries.title: PHX C.A.R.E.S. — street outreach
entries.description:
Phone: 602-262-6251, then press 6. Published request hours: Monday–Saturday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Request outreach for someone living outside or report an encampment. Give an exact location and describe urgent health or safety needs. Outreach cannot force a person to accept services and does not guarantee a shelter bed. Homelessness itself is not a crime; call 911 for immediate danger.
City of Phoenix — coordinated homeless response

entries.title: Heat safety and current seasonal status
entries.description:
Current status: Phoenix's dedicated 2026 heat-relief sites closed for the season on October 1, 2026. Do not travel to the former 24-hour site at 20 W. Jackson Street expecting it to be open. Phoenix Public Library locations continue to offer air-conditioned space during normal hours. Call 211 for a current open location.
The regional Heat Relief Network normally operates May 1–September 30. Check the live network before relying on any seasonal site or extended hours.
City of Phoenix — 2026 heat-site closure notice | MAG Heat Relief Network — https://web-prod.phoenix.gov/newsroom/heat-news/heat-relief-sites-open-may-1.html

entries.title: Heat illness — act early
entries.description:
Move to shade or air conditioning, loosen clothing, cool the skin, and sip water if the person is awake and able to swallow. Confusion, fainting, seizures, very hot skin, or inability to drink can mean heat stroke: call 911 and cool the person while help is coming.
Maricopa County — heat-relief toolkit

entries.title: 988 and Arizona crisis support
entries.description:
Call or text: 988. Arizona statewide line: 844-534-HOPE (4673), 24 hours.
Free, confidential crisis support for suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, mental-health crisis, or urgent substance-use concerns. Call 911 when there is immediate physical danger.
Solari Crisis Response Network

entries.title: Arizona 211
entries.description:
Call: 211 or 877-211-8661.
Ask for an open shelter access point, meal, cooling location, health service, benefit office, or transport option. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and confirm details directly with the provider.
211 Arizona

entries.title: A practical plan for today
entries.description:
1. Handle danger first. Call 911 for immediate danger, serious illness, heat stroke, or overdose. Use 988 for a mental-health or substance-use crisis.
2. Use the right shelter route. Single adults: Welcome Center. Families: 211 or Family Housing Hub. Ages 12–17: Safe Place. Ages 18–24: HomeBase. Veterans: VA center. Domestic violence: the confidential screening line.
3. Protect against heat. Dedicated 2026 heat sites are closed for the season, but dangerous heat can occur outside it. Use a library during normal hours or call 211 for an open indoor location.
4. Secure food and hygiene. Check André House, St. Vincent de Paul, NourishPHX, Key Campus, or Justa Center according to your age and today's schedule.
5. Protect documents and medication. Keep papers dry, photograph them if safe, write down medication names, and ask about secure mail or storage. Do not use a mailing address without permission.
6. Start benefits and ID work early. Use Health-e-Arizona Plus, Homeless ID Project, and a caseworker. Ask what alternate proof is accepted.
7. Ask precise questions. “Is intake open now?”, “Can I enter today?”, “What ID is required?”, “Is there a fee?”, “Can you accommodate my disability, service animal, pet, medication, partner, or children?”, and “What should I do if there is no space?”
8. Keep a second plan. Write down at least two options, the name of the person you spoke with, and the time to call back. Availability can change before you arrive.
Help improve this page: report a closed service, changed phone number, or missing local resource through the project repository. Do not publish a survivor's location, private medical information, or another person's personal details.
No Home Help on GitHub | Contribution guide — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md

entries.title: Brian Garcia Welcome Center — single adults
entries.description:
Call before traveling: 602-883-4509. Campus line: 602-229-5155.
The facility is open 24 hours. Keys to Change publishes assessment and service-plan hours of 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Staff can assess needs and discuss CASS, Respiro, other shelter, benefits, health care, and housing navigation. A visit does not guarantee placement.
Keys to Change — get help
entries.address: Address: 206 S. 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: Central Arizona Shelter Services — adults age 18+
entries.description:
Shelter information: 602-229-5155. CASS main office: 602-256-6945.
Single-adult beds are assigned through in-person intake, first come and first served. CASS does not reserve beds by phone or email. Bring photo ID, medications, and useful documents if you have them, but ask for document-replacement help if you do not. People age 55+ can ask about The Haven, which is referral based.
CASS — get help
entries.address: Start at: Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S. 12th Avenue

entries.title: Family Housing Hub — families with a child under 18
entries.description:
Start with 211. Direct line: 602-595-8700. TDD: 602-759-1896.
This is the regional entry route for families with dependent children. A waiting list may be used. Explain the household size, children's ages, pregnancy, immediate safety, disability or medical needs, and whether you have transport. Do not go to CASS expecting family intake.
UMOM — find help

entries.title: Halle Women's Center — single women without children
entries.description:
Waitlist: 602-362-5833.
Call about the current waitlist, intake, eligibility, and what to do tonight if no space is available. A call does not reserve a bed.
UMOM — find help
entries.address: Address: 3424 E. Van Buren Street, Phoenix, AZ 85008

entries.title: HomeBase — young adults ages 18–24
entries.description:
Phone intake: 602-263-5531.
Emergency shelter and a weekday drop-in center. The provider publishes drop-in hours Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m., with showers, laundry, food, rest space, and case management. Call about shelter intake and current capacity.
Native American Connections — youth housing
entries.address: Address: 931 E. Devonshire Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85014

entries.title: Safe Place — youth ages 12–17
entries.description:
24-hour phone: 602-841-5799. Text: send SAFE and your address to 44357.
Ask for immediate safety planning and youth shelter help. If a young person is in immediate danger, call 911.
MAG — help by household type

entries.title: Phoenix Rescue Mission
entries.description:
Help and program intake: 602-233-3000. Street outreach: 602-346-3361.
Street outreach, basic supplies, recovery programs, and residential program screening. The men's Transforming Lives Center is at 1801 S. 35th Avenue; the women's and children's Changing Lives Center is at 338 N. 15th Avenue. These are structured Christian recovery programs, not guaranteed walk-in emergency beds. Call first about requirements.
Phoenix Rescue Mission — get help

entries.title: Referral-only options
entries.description:
Safe Outdoor Space, the Navigation Center, and Respiro generally use referrals and are not reliable public walk-in options. Ask the Welcome Center, PHX C.A.R.E.S., or an outreach worker whether a referral is appropriate and currently available.
City of Phoenix — homeless solutions | Keys to Change — Key Campus — https://www.phoenix.gov/administration/departments/homeless-solutions.html

entries.title: André House — dinner
entries.description:
Phone: 602-255-0580. Published dinner: Saturday–Thursday, 5:00–6:00 p.m.; line begins at 4:00 p.m.
Community dinner and basic services. André House is Catholic and says it welcomes every person. Check the current weekly calendar before a long trip.
André House — services
entries.address: Address: 213 S. 11th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: St. Vincent de Paul — Phoenix Dining Room
entries.description:
Program phone: 602-261-6805. Published meals: breakfast Monday–Friday, 7:00–8:00 a.m.; lunch daily, 11:00 a.m.–12:45 p.m.; dinner Friday, 4:00–5:00 p.m.
Walk-in adult dining room. Seasonal afternoon heat relief runs June 1–September 30 and is closed now. St. Vincent de Paul is Catholic; its meal page does not state that worship is required.
St. Vincent de Paul — Phoenix Dining Room
entries.address: Address: 1075 W. Jackson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: St. Vincent de Paul — Family Evening Meal
entries.description:
Phone: 602-850-6901. Published meal: Monday–Friday, 4:00–6:00 p.m.
For families accompanied by a child under 18. Call about current access before traveling.
St. Vincent de Paul — meals and food boxes
entries.address: Address: 420 W. Watkins Road, Phoenix, AZ 85003

entries.title: NourishPHX — emergency food and clothing
entries.description:
Phone: 602-254-7450. Published emergency-service hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00–11:00 a.m.; weekends closed.
No appointment is listed. Bring ID if you have it. Ask what alternatives are accepted if you have no ID and whether any clothing fee applies to your household.
NourishPHX — contact and hours
entries.address: Address: 501 S. 9th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: St. Mary's Food Bank — Phoenix Food Center

Phone: 602-242-3663. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m.
Call or check the current distribution calendar and ask about household, ZIP code, ID, and frequency rules before traveling.
St. Mary's Food Bank — locations
entries.address: Address: 3131 W. Thomas Road, Phoenix, AZ 85017

entries.title: Find food open today
entries.description:
Call 211 or 877-211-8661. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets, household size, transport limits, and dietary or mobility needs. Confirm the schedule with the provider.
211 Arizona

categories.title: Showers, laundry, clothing, mail, and storage

entries.title: Lodestar Day Resource Center — Key Campus
entries.description:
Campus phone: 602-229-5155.
Day room, navigation, benefit partners, showers, limited clothing, storage, mail, document help, and other scheduled services. Individual services have different hours and some are first come, first served. Call or ask the Welcome Center for the current schedule.
Key Campus — service map and schedule
entries.address: Address: 1125 W. Jackson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: Key Campus mail
entries.description:
Ask the mailroom before using this address. Confirm that you are registered, the exact name format, accepted items, collection hours, ID rules, and how long mail is held. Do not send important documents until staff confirms the procedure.
Keys to Change — Key Campus
entries.address: Mail service address: 232 S. 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: André House — showers, laundry, clothing, and hygiene
entries.description:
Phone: 602-255-0580.
Published services: showers Monday–Thursday, 12:30–3:00 p.m.; laundry Monday–Wednesday, 8:30 a.m.–12:00 p.m., with limited slots and an earlier line; clothing Tuesday and Thursday, 12:30–3:00 p.m., and Saturday, 1:00–3:00 p.m.; hygiene supplies on selected afternoons. Arrive early and check for closures.
André House — current services
entries.address: Address: 213 S. 11th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: Justa Center — adults age 55 and older
entries.description:
Main phone: 602-254-6524. Intake appointment: 602-313-3858.
Showers, laundry, hygiene items, meals, lockers, mail, document storage, computers, benefits help, health services, and housing navigation for people age 55+. Intake is published daily from 7:00–9:00 a.m.; walk-in space is limited. Normal hours are 7:00 a.m.–2:30 p.m.; extended summer hours end after October.
Justa Center — day center
entries.address: Address: 1001 W. Jefferson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: CASS — services for shelter guests
entries.description:
Phone: 602-256-6945.
Shelter guests receive meals, hygiene, showers, restrooms, case management, and secure mail. Some services may have limited access for people not staying there; call first rather than assuming walk-in access.
CASS — get help
entries.address: Address: 230 S. 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

categories.title: Health, dental, mental health, and substance-use help

entries.title: Circle the City — Downtown Family Health Center
entries.description:
Phone: 602-258-8282. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; weekends, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed 12:00–1:00 p.m.
Primary and preventive care for people experiencing homelessness, including chronic-disease care, immunizations, behavioral-health and substance-use consultation, case management, and care coordination. Walk-ins and appointments are supported; call about current access.
Circle the City — outpatient care
entries.address: Address: 220 S. 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: Circle the City — Parsons Family Health Center
entries.description:
Phone: 602-776-7676. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed 12:00–1:00 p.m.
Primary, preventive, behavioral-health, substance-use, case-management, and pediatric care. Call about walk-ins, appointments, cost, insurance, and documents.
Circle the City — locations and hours
entries.address: Address: 3522 N. 3rd Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85013

entries.title: Mobile medical care and medical respite
entries.description:
Mobile schedule: 602-516-6825. Downtown Medical Respite: 210 S. 12th Avenue, 602-254-4282.
Medical respite is short-term clinical recovery for eligible people referred after illness, injury, or hospital care. It is not a public walk-in shelter and does not guarantee acceptance.
Circle the City — contacts

entries.title: Brighter Way Dental Center
entries.description:
General phone: 602-362-0744.
Dental care for adults experiencing homelessness, veterans, and low-income older adults. Treatment fees apply; any assistance is assessed separately. Confirm intake, appointment availability, fees, and eligibility before traveling.
Brighter Way — current dental information
entries.address: Address: 230 S. 12th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: Solari Warm Line — peer support before a crisis
entries.description:
Phone: 602-347-1100, 24 hours.
Free, confidential peer support for adults age 18+ dealing with loneliness, mental-health concerns, substance use, or recovery. Use 988 for a crisis and 911 for immediate danger.
Solari — Warm Line

entries.title: Naloxone and safer-use supplies
entries.description:
Sonoran Prevention Works publishes current outreach sites and ways to obtain naloxone. Schedules change, so contact the listed provider before traveling. Pharmacies may also dispense naloxone under Arizona's standing order; call first about stock and cost.
If someone may be overdosing, call 911, give naloxone if available, and stay with the person. More than one dose may be needed.
Sonoran Prevention Works — get supplies | Arizona naloxone information — https://spwaz.org/arizonanaloxone/

entries.title: Valley Metro
entries.description:
Customer service: 602-253-5000.
Call for routes, first and last trips, fares, accessibility, and service changes. Exact cash is needed on buses and drivers do not give change. Do not board without confirming the current fare or a valid pass.
Valley Metro — hours and customer service

entries.title: Valley Metro reduced fare
entries.description:
Reduced fare is available on local bus and light rail for youth ages 6–18, adults age 65+, Medicare cardholders, and eligible people with disabilities. Proof and an application are required; approval is not immediate.
Disability applications: Valley Metro Mobility Center, 4600 E. Washington Street, Suite 101. Phone: 602-253-5000, option 3.
Valley Metro — reduced-fare rules

entries.title: Phoenix Public Library — computers, Wi-Fi, and cooling
entries.description:
Library information: 602-262-4636. Burton Barr Central Library: 1221 N. Central Avenue.
Libraries provide air-conditioned space during normal hours, public Wi-Fi, and computer access. Ask about guest computer access, card requirements, printing, scanning, charging, and current branch hours. Burton Barr has construction and service changes during 2025–26, so call before traveling.
Phoenix Public Library — computers and internet

entries.title: Transportation from Key Campus
entries.description:
The campus service map lists Elaine transportation on a schedule. It is not an on-demand or guaranteed ride. Ask the Welcome Center or Lodestar Day Resource Center about current destinations, eligibility, pickup times, and capacity.
Key Campus — service map

entries.title: Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport
entries.description:
The free PHX Sky Train connects Terminals 3 and 4 with the Valley Metro Rail station at 44th Street and Washington Street. Valley Metro fare is required for the light-rail portion. Check route and operating information before relying on a late-night connection.
An airport is not a shelter. Remaining in terminals without a travel purpose may lead to contact with airport staff or police. If you need shelter, use 211 or the Welcome Center before going to the airport.
Phoenix Sky Harbor — PHX Sky Train | Valley Metro — https://www.skyharbor.com/ground-transportation/phx-sky-train/

entries.title: Tickets and travel help
entries.description: Do not assume a shelter, outreach team, church, or city office will buy a ticket. If safe reunification is possible, ask a caseworker whether a verified transportation program exists and what proof is needed. Never hand identity documents or money to an unofficial broker.

categories.title: Benefits, housing, rent, and utility help

entries.title: Health-e-Arizona Plus — AHCCCS, SNAP, and cash assistance
entries.description:
Phone: 855-432-7587, Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
Apply for Arizona Medicaid health coverage, Nutrition Assistance, and Cash Assistance; renew benefits; report changes; and ask for application help. The online portal has had service interruptions in 2026, so use the phone line or ask a community-assistor organization if the site is unavailable.
AHCCCS — Health-e-Arizona Plus

entries.title: Phoenix Family Services Centers — crisis assistance
entries.description:
Phone: 602-534-AIDE (2433).
Ask about current emergency rent, mortgage, or utility assistance, case management, and eligibility. Funding and appointment availability change and are not guaranteed.
John F. Long: 3454 N. 51st Avenue. Sunnyslope: 914 W. Hatcher Road. Travis L. Williams: 4732 S. Central Avenue.
City of Phoenix — crisis assistance

entries.title: Coordinated Entry and housing assessment
entries.description:
Single adults can begin at the Welcome Center; families should use the Family Housing Hub; young adults ages 18–24 should use a youth access point; veterans should use the VA Community Resource and Referral Center. Assessment does not guarantee a housing voucher, apartment, or shelter bed.
Keys to Change — coordinated access | MAG — need help — https://azmag.gov/Programs/Community-Initiatives/Homelessness/Need-Help

entries.title: Preventing eviction — act before the court date
entries.description:
Call the Phoenix crisis-assistance line and Community Legal Services as soon as you receive a notice. Keep the notice, lease, payment records, messages, identification, and proof of income. Do not ignore court papers. Assistance and representation depend on eligibility, deadlines, and capacity.
City of Phoenix — service and eviction-help brochure

entries.title: ARIZONA@WORK — City of Phoenix
entries.description:
South Job Center: 4635 S. Central Avenue, 602-495-6905. West Job Center: 3406 N. 51st Avenue, 602-495-6906.
Job-search help, computers, career planning, training referrals, résumé assistance, adult education, reentry, youth, and vocational-rehabilitation partner services. Call for current hours, orientation, required documents, and the best center for your needs. Services do not guarantee employment.
ARIZONA@WORK — Phoenix locations

entries.title: St. Joseph the Worker
entries.description:
Phone: 602-417-9854.
Employment support for people facing barriers, including job search, résumé and interview help, work clothing or tools when available, and employment planning. Call about orientation, eligibility, current hours, and documents. Assistance does not guarantee a job or financial help.
St. Joseph the Worker
entries.address: Address: 1125 W. Jackson Street, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: NourishPHX Job and Resource Center
entries.description:
Job appointments: 602-775-5744.
Ask about job-search help, résumés, applications, computers, interview preparation, and current appointment availability.
NourishPHX — contact
entries.address: Address: 501 S. 9th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85007

entries.title: Phoenix Public Library
entries.description:
Use public computers and Wi-Fi for applications and email. Ask staff about guest access, printing, scanning, résumé resources, and current workforce programs.
Phoenix Public Library — computers and internet

entries.title: Community Legal Services — civil legal aid
entries.description:
Phone intake: 602-258-3434, Monday–Friday, 9:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m. Toll-free: 800-852-9075.
Legal aid may cover eviction, housing, benefits, consumer, family, farmworker, and other civil matters. Income and case eligibility apply. The central office currently limits walk-ins because of building repairs, so apply by phone or online unless the provider confirms otherwise.
Community Legal Services — current access
entries.address: Central Phoenix mailing address: 305 S. 2nd Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85003

entries.title: City of Phoenix eviction legal services
entries.description:
Phone: 602-262-7210.
Ask about current eviction legal assistance and document drop-off through Phoenix Family Services Centers. Keep every notice and court paper and call immediately; deadlines can be very short. Help depends on eligibility and capacity.
City of Phoenix — services and eviction help

entries.title: Friendly House — immigration legal services
entries.description:
Phone: 602-416-7200.
Affordable immigration consultations and representation for family petitions, DACA, VAWA, U and T visas, green-card renewals, and citizenship. Call about fees, appointments, language access, and documents. Services and outcomes are not guaranteed.
Friendly House — immigration legal services
entries.address: Address: 802 S. 1st Avenue, Suite 1, Phoenix, AZ 85003

entries.title: Homeless Court at Key Campus
entries.description:
Phone: 602-342-6952.
The campus map lists Homeless Court on selected Tuesdays and Thursdays. Call first to confirm the schedule, eligible cases, referral requirements, documents, and whether you must already be working with a case manager.
Key Campus — service map

entries.title: Homeless ID Project — Arizona ID and birth certificates
entries.description:
Phone: 602-223-3427. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.; closed the second Wednesday and third Monday of each month; first come, first served.
Help obtaining Arizona identification and birth certificates. Arrive early and ask what proof is needed, which states are covered, whether fees apply, and how documents will be delivered.
Homeless ID Project — Phoenix service
entries.address: Address: 1125 W. Jackson Street, inside the Lodestar Day Resource Center

entries.title: Arizona identification card
entries.description:
A standard Arizona ID generally costs $12 and requires proof of identity, a Social Security number, and two proofs of Arizona residency. People age 65+, SSI recipients, and eligible homeless veterans may qualify for a no-fee card. A standard ID is not a federal REAL ID.
Ask Homeless ID Project or a caseworker to identify acceptable documents and residency evidence before visiting MVD.
Arizona MVD — identification card requirements

entries.title: Maricopa County Vital Records — Arizona birth certificate
entries.description:
Phone: 602-506-6805. Published hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; Wednesday, 9:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
A certified Arizona birth certificate is listed at $20. Eligibility, application, and identity requirements apply. Use Homeless ID Project first if you lack the required ID or fee.
Maricopa County — Vital Records
entries.address: Phoenix office: 1645 E. Roosevelt Street, Phoenix, AZ 85006

entries.title: Social Security
entries.description:
National phone: 800-772-1213. Ask about replacing a Social Security card, updating a record, SSI or SSDI, and the nearest office. Do not pay an unofficial website for a replacement card.
Social Security Administration — replace a card

categories.title: Women, domestic violence, trafficking, and LGBTQ+ support

entries.title: Domestic-violence shelter screening
entries.description:
24-hour central line: 480-890-3039 or 844-SAFE-DVS (723-3387).
Confidential safety planning and screening for domestic-violence shelter. Call from a safe phone if possible. Shelter addresses may be confidential and space is not guaranteed. Call 911 for immediate danger.
UMOM — domestic-violence access | MAG — need help — https://azmag.gov/Programs/Community-Initiatives/Homelessness/Need-Help

entries.title: Arizona Coalition to End Sexual and Domestic Violence
entries.description:
Legal advocacy: 602-279-2900 or 800-782-6400. TTY: 602-279-7270.
Information, safety planning, referrals, and legal advocacy for survivors. It is not a shelter-placement guarantee.
ACESDV — get help

entries.title: Human trafficking help
entries.description:
National hotline: 888-373-7888. Text: 233733. Phoenix Family Advocacy Center: 602-534-2120.
Use a safe device if someone monitors your phone. Ask for a safe plan, emergency referral, and language assistance. Call 911 if you are in immediate danger.
National Human Trafficking Hotline

entries.title: one·n·ten — LGBTQ+ youth and young adults
entries.description:
Phone: 602-400-2601.
Affirming programs, basic resources, community support, and housing assistance for LGBTQ+ youth and young adults. Call about age limits, drop-in times, current housing navigation, and what is available today. This is not a guaranteed emergency shelter bed.
one·n·ten — programs
entries.address: Downtown Youth Center: 1101 N. Central Avenue, Suite 104, Phoenix, AZ 85004

categories.title: Families, youth, older adults, and disability needs

entries.title: Families with dependent children
entries.description:
Start with 211. Family Housing Hub: 602-595-8700.
Ask about shelter assessment, the waitlist, documents, transport, school continuity, food, diapers, medical needs, and what to do tonight. Keep the phone available for callbacks if possible.
UMOM — family housing access

entries.title: Young people
entries.description:
Ages 12–17: Safe Place, 602-841-5799, 24 hours. Ages 18–24: HomeBase, 602-263-5531.
Youth services may help with shelter, showers, laundry, meals, school or employment, documents, health care, and housing navigation. Explain immediate safety, age, pregnancy, trafficking risk, LGBTQ+ safety concerns, and whether an adult controls your documents or phone.
MAG — youth access | Native American Connections — HomeBase — https://www.nativeconnections.org/housing/youth/

entries.title: Adults age 55 and older
entries.description:
Justa Center: 602-254-6524. 24-hour Senior Help Line: 602-264-4357.
Justa Center provides day services and housing navigation for people age 55+. The Senior Help Line can screen for older-adult services, caregiver help, benefits, and the DOVES domestic-violence program. Ask the Welcome Center about The Haven shelter referral.
Justa Center

entries.title: Disability and access needs
entries.description:
Tell every access point about wheelchair or walker use, oxygen, medication refrigeration, communication needs, service animals, inability to stand in line, or need for an accessible bed or restroom. Ask for a reasonable accommodation and accessible transport.
For Valley Metro reduced fare and paratransit information, call 602-253-5000. For benefit screening and long-term-care questions, call 855-432-7587.
Valley Metro — reduced fare | AHCCCS — contacts — https://azahcccs.gov/shared/AHCCCScontacts.html

entries.title: VA Community Resource and Referral Center
entries.description:
Phone: 602-248-6040. Published hours: Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
Coordinated access for veterans experiencing homelessness, including assessment, health and benefit connections, outreach, housing programs, and referrals. Bring military or identity documents if available, but call even if they are missing. Placement and financial help are not guaranteed.
Keys to Change — veteran access
entries.address: Address: 1500 E. Thomas Road, Suite 106, rear of building, Phoenix, AZ 85014

entries.title: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans
entries.description:
Phone: 877-424-3838, 24 hours.
For veterans who are homeless or at risk and people calling on their behalf. Ask about local VA outreach, shelter, housing, medical care, and benefits.
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — homeless veteran call center

entries.title: Arizona ID fee waiver
entries.description:
Arizona MVD may waive the fee for an eligible homeless veteran. MVD verifies veteran status and may require a recent homelessness statement from VA or a verified provider. Ask the VA center or Homeless ID Project to prepare the correct paperwork first.
Arizona MVD — ID fee information

entries.title: Ask before traveling with an animal
entries.description: Tell the shelter whether the animal is a trained service animal, emotional-support animal, or pet; species and size; vaccination status; crate or leash; and whether temporary foster care would be acceptable. Policies and space differ. Do not abandon an animal because one program says no.

entries.title: The Arizona Pet Project
entries.description:
Phone: 602-882-8627. The office is not open to the public and is not an animal shelter.
Request assistance for pet food, veterinary barriers, housing problems, domestic-violence safety, or another crisis that could separate you from a pet. Help depends on eligibility and capacity.
Arizona Pet Project — human services | Pet food and resources — https://azpetproject.org/resources/community-resources/

entries.title: Temporary pet care and food
entries.description:
The Arizona Pet Project lists Helping Hands for Homeless Hounds at 602-410-0983 and Lost Our Home Pet Rescue at 602-445-7387. Call first: an application, appointment, geographic limit, or waitlist may apply.
Arizona Pet Project — pet housing resources
